item.text:
Report updated. Summary of this continuation:

**New work this turn**
- Confirmed the sandbox blocks AF_INET outright (`socket()` → EPERM; AF_UNIX works), so the TCP transport tests and the TCP-gated integration tests (`TestRaft_Integ`) genuinely cannot run in my shell, and the `isolated_exec` MCP tool still isn't dispatchable from my side. Recorded as a hard limitation.
- Checked the work tree's `.git` for any independent baseline object — empty, nothing to compare against.
- Wrote and ran an independent crash/restart stress test, [zz_audit_crash_test.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-08_19-48-15-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/zz_audit_crash_test.go) (`TestAudit_CrashRestartFollower`, in-memory transport): each round applies entries, crash-shuts-down a follower, keeps committing without it, restarts it on the same durable stores, and requires full reconvergence with no committed entry lost.

**Result:** 3/3 PASS (~10.5s each) and PASS under `-race` with no data races — a positive, reproducible crash-fault-tolerance check.

**Honest caveat:** my first version of that harness (replacing the crashed node's transport) stalled. That was a defect in *my* test setup, not the implementation — the library's own multi-node restart tests build a fresh transport for a new single-node env rather than re-inserting a node into a live cluster; reusing the un-closed in-memory transport made it deterministic. I recorded this plainly in the report rather than dressing it up as a finding.

**Standing verdict unchanged:** the captured tree is byte-identical to the official `hashicorp/raft@v1.7.3` module content, the in-repo suite passes (173 pass; only AF_INET transport tests blocked), `go vet`/`gofmt` clean, and no concrete correctness defect has been found. Report: [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-08_19-48-15-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md); logs under `work/logs/`.

Next useful step if continued: get `isolated_exec` working (or dependency zips for `raft-boltdb`/`bolt`) to run the TCP transport suite and the `fuzzy` linearizability tests — the only remaining coverage gaps.
